title: Allen's Brass Band, the old Eureka and Big Landry's E-flat cornet
summary: Ernie's most organized brass band was old man Allen's. He also played funerals with the old Eureka under Big Landry, who played a loud E-flat cornet to the end.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Is there anything about the different bands, the brass bands that you've played in, that you could tell us? Any organized band or just different make-up bands?
No, no, I played in the most organized band that I played in, the brass band, was with old man Allen, Red Allen's daddy. Allen's brass band.
Did you have any other name for his band?

No, his name was Allen's brass band, Allen's brass band. That was his name. Quite natural. I played plenty of funerals with the old Eureka. But I mean, before they had this group, I mean, when they had Dajama playing trumpet group, Mama Dajama, and T-Boy Remy, and First Humphrey, and several other older guys that did, see. And at that time, this guy named him again, Big Landry was the leader of that band. Now he was the only, he was the last trumpet player around there, playing in, he was in a parade that was playing an E-flat cornet like Manny Parade. Landry played an E-flat?
You could hear him for blocks.
That's the same man that died about 1949 played a big iron down there.
That's right, played with Big Al Lewis and Big Ralph. Well, Rodgers was the snare drum player in that band then. Well, that was the band that I played. Well, they had a...
How late did he use that E-flat? I've never seen it.
Until he died. Really on the bridge. He used it down there. I don't know him to have no other trumpet.
He used to use the Holy Ghost's bar, I play when I was playing. Sure. He'd play a solo trumpet. No, I didn't know. And he, that was a powerful man.
